battle.name: 臨安之戰
battle.brief: 德祐二年（1276）三月，伯顏率元軍主力沿江順流而下，取潭州、鄂州後直抵南宋行在臨安，圍城數月，宋廷遣使議和不成，守將范文虎以城降，謝太后奉恭帝出降，元軍入皇城。卡面配重投石車即元軍「回回砲」一類攻城器，襄陽之戰後隨軍東下，在江南攻城序列中壓制城牆角樓、掩護雲梯登城。

kit.name: 配重投石車
kit.history: 長臂配重把石頭甩過城牆。工程比攻城武器更早決定勝負。

countries: 交戰雙方是元朝的江南征討軍與南宋行在朝廷系統下的兩浙官軍、淮南軍與各地勤王師。元方以伯顏領銜的建康行中書省為最高節制：至元十二年（1275）忽必烈在北方平定昔里吉之亂、重開南征之後，先命伯顏自建康分兵三路南攻，又令伯顏回上都陳述軍情，待七月下定滅宋決心，才命伯顏為建康行中書省右丞相，率主力直取臨安；命平章政事阿里海牙領兵攻湖南、淮揚，阻止淮東宋軍南援；命左副都元帥李恆、漢軍萬戶武秀與張榮實取江西，斷南宋東西聯繫。元軍兵種由蒙古騎兵、漢軍降卒（宋地歸附的步卒與攻城匠）、沿江水師舟楫，以及配帶西域回回砲手的攻城部隊拼成，糧秣器械多自江西、湖廣經河道轉運，軍令由中書省、行省與各路萬戶逐級分派。宋方則是南宋最後的中央朝廷：行在臨安的樞密院、兩浙路兵馬與臨安守軍，屯於揚州、真州、淮東的淮南制置司軍，以及張世傑、文天祥等奉詔北上的勤王師。編制上宋軍以江淮前線為第一道拒止，臨安本身則以皇城、內城、外城三重城垣，加上城內縱橫河道與江南運河構成的水陸互援網為依託，全國漕運終點、財賦與兵源都集中於此。雙方爭的不是一座城，而是兩浙、江南、淮南三路的財賦與天下正統的名分。
countriesEn: The two sides were the Yuan army campaigning through Jiangnan and the Southern Song's own armies in the Two Rivers region, in Huainan and in the relief columns that mustered from across the empire. On the Yuan side the highest authority was the Jianggan Branch Secretariat headed by Bayan: in 1275, the twelfth year of the Zhiyuan era, after Kublai Khan had pacified the revolt of Shiregi in the north and reopened the southern campaign, Bayan was first sent to divide his force at Jianggan into three columns marching south, and was then summoned back to Shangdu to report on the state of the war; only in the seventh month, once Kublai had made up his mind to destroy the Song, was Bayan appointed right chancellor of the Jianggan Branch Secretariat and ordered to lead the main force straight at Lin'an. Ariq Qoshqar, the commissioner of the Secretariat, was given the armies for Hunan and for Huaiyang so as to block any Song relief from coming south out of Huaidong; the left deputy commander-in-chief Li Heng and the Han commanders of ten thousand men, Wu Xiu and Zhang Rongshi, were sent into Jiangxi to sever the Song's eastern and western connections. The Yuan army was pieced together from Mongol cavalry, Han troops who had surrendered out of Song territory (both foot soldiers and siege engineers), river flotillas moving down the Yangtze, and assault detachments equipped with the trebuchets worked by Muslim engineers from the west; grain and matériel came mostly by water out of Jiangxi and Huguang, and orders passed down in steps from the Central Secretariat through the branch administrations to the commanders of ten thousand. On the Song side lay the last central government of the Southern Song: the Privy Council and the Two Rivers military administration sitting in Lin'an with the city garrison, the Huai Southern Circuit troops stationed at Yangzhou, Zhenjiang and Huai-dong, and the relief columns raised by Zhang Shijie, Wen Tianxiang and others in obedience to the court's summons. Structurally the Song relied on the river front as its first line of refusal, while Lin'an itself rested on three concentric circuits of defence — the imperial city, the inner city and the outer city — together with the network of canals and streets inside the walls, which let the city feed itself by water and land alike; the terminus of the empire's grain transport, its revenues and its man-power all lay in this one place. What the two sides fought over was not a single walled town but the revenues of the Two Rivers, Jiangnan and Huainan, and the claim to be the legitimate order of the realm.
people: 全場最關鍵的名字是伯顏八剌。1275年元軍攻下建康府與鎮江府、乘勝追擊之際，忽必烈因北方昔里吉之亂而令大軍暫停南下，伯顏奉詔回上都面陳軍情，七月中下旬忽必烈才定下乘勝滅宋的決心，重派伯顏統軍南下。臨安出降之後，伯顏以朝廷名義招撫兩浙各州縣，約束軍士不得侵擾居民，宣布降民可以繳錢贖身而不至淪為奴隸，這套「不掠、不擄」的軍令，使元軍在江南的接管遠比一般征服順利。元方另有平章政事阿里海牙攻湖南與淮揚，左副都元帥李恆、漢軍萬戶武秀與張榮實取江西，替伯顏拉出一張從江西到淮東的網。宋方主持者是右丞相賈似道，他以樞密院權柄總攝軍務：一面遣將士赴寧波、鎮江一線迎敵，一面在德祐元年冬遣使赴元營議和，暗中奉上傳國玉璽與降表；元軍不受，反責玉璽為偽，議和破裂後賈似道棄軍逃往揚州，為部將所誅。臨安守將范文虎在圍城之後以城降元，開城迎宋廷出降。行在方面是謝太后與年幼的宋恭帝，最後由謝太后奉國璽與二王出降。張世傑率兩浙兵北上，曾在焦山以水軍列陣挽回局勢，一炬而潰，收拾散卒再起；文天祥自江西率勤王師入衛，兵敗被俘，拒降不屈，三年後死於大都。收尾一幕則是陸秀夫背著宋少帝投海，宋室至此終絕。
peopleEn: The name that governs the whole campaign is Bayan of the Baarin. In 1275, after the Yuan had taken the prefectures of Jianggan and Zhenjiang and was in pursuit, Kublai halted the advance because of the revolt of Shiregi in the north, and Bayan was summoned back to Shangdu to report on the state of the war; only in the seventh month, when Kublai resolved to finish the Song while the momentum was with him, was Bayan sent south again to command. After Lin'an surrendered he went on to pacify the prefectures and counties of the Two Rivers in the name of the court, forbade his soldiers to rob the populace, and proclaimed that those who surrendered could redeem themselves by payment of money rather than fall into slavery. That discipline — no plunder, no capture — made the Yuan takeover of Jiangnan far smoother than conquests usually are. On the Yuan side there were also Ariq Qoshqar, commissioner of the Secretariat, in Hunan and Huaiyang, and the left deputy commander-in-chief Li Heng with the Han commanders of ten thousand men, Wu Xiu and Zhang Rongshi, in Jiangxi, who drew a net from Jiangxi to Huaidong for Bayan. On the Song side the man in charge was the right chancellor Jia Sidao, who held the authority of the Privy Council over military operations: on the one hand he sent troops forward to the Ningbo and Zhenjiang line to meet the enemy, on the other, in the winter of the first year of the Deyou era, he dispatched envoys to the Yuan camp to treat, and behind their backs handed over the imperial seal and a letter of submission. The Yuan refused them and declared the seal a forgery; once the negotiation collapsed Jia Sidao abandoned the army and fled to Yangzhou, where his own men killed him. The commander of Lin'an, Fan Wenhu, surrendered the city to the Yuan once the siege had closed in and opened the gates to receive the Song court. On the court side were Empress Dowager Xie and the child Emperor Gong, and it was the empress dowager who finally came out with the state seal and the two princes. Zhang Shijie led the Two Rivers troops north and tried to reverse the situation at Jiao Mountain with a fleet deployed on the water, only for it to be burned and scattered; he gathered the survivors and rose again. Wen Tianxiang marched a relief column in from Jiangxi, was defeated and taken, refused to surrender, and was put to death three years later at Dadu. The last scene belongs to Lu Xiufu, who carried the young Song emperor into the sea, and with that the Song house came to its end.
kits: 卡面這件配重投石車在這場戰役裡的位置，是元軍攻城序列中最重的一門器械，也就是中國史籍所稱的「回回砲」。這類器械原出歐洲與西亞的攻城傳統，元軍在十三世紀的西征中把西域工匠帶回的技術帶到東方，襄陽之戰（1272至1273年）時元軍以回回砲攻破樊城，砲石重逾百斤，一擊可入地數尺，此後它便成為元軍攻城裝備的制式配備。配重投石車的優點是射程遠、可以從攻城器械本身無法靠近的距離外打擊城頭守軍與角樓，投石可越過城牆直接落在城內或城頭通道上，掩護雲梯與撞竿接近；缺點同樣明顯：機械龐大、運轉遲緩、發射間隔長、必須固定在炮位上，因此必須在開戰前先選定高處或砲舟，把整個攻城序列拉長。此外它完全不具備破城牆本體的能力，擊毀角樓、門樓、打亂城頭佈防已是極限，真正的破城仍要靠雲梯、撞竿、填壕與內應。臨安之役的逐門記載並不完整，可以確定的是元軍自襄陽、鄂州一路帶下的攻城器械序列與襄陽時並無二致，重型投石車必在其中；宋軍的反制則是城頭弓弩、檑木滾石、撞竿破門與火藥箭、火藥桶一類火器，《宋史·兵志》所載「突火槍」即襄陽攻城時已試用、以火藥推送箭矢的攻城火器，到此役仍是守城方對付攻城器械與密集人馬的手段。除攻城器外，元軍還有蒙古彎弓、標槍、馬刀、札甲與鎖子甲，漢軍攜帶的床子弩與神臂弓，以及沿江運行的平底沙船、鬥艦與載糧漕船，陸上則靠牛車與驛站「站赤」接力轉運。
kitsEn: The place of the counterweight trebuchet on this card in this campaign is as the heaviest single engine in the Yuan siege sequence, the weapon Chinese records call the huihui pao, the Muslim trebuchet. The type belongs to the siege tradition of Europe and West Asia; the Yuan brought the craft of western craftsmen back from the west during the campaigns of the thirteenth century, and at Xiangyang in 1272 and 1273 the Yuan used the huihui pao to break Fancheng, the stones weighing more than a hundred jin and sinking several chi into the ground with a single blow. From then on the engine became standard equipment in Yuan siege trains. Its strengths are range and the ability to strike the defenders and the corner towers from a distance that the rest of the siege train can never approach: the stones clear the wall and land in the city or on the wall-walk, covering the ladders and rams as they come in. Its weaknesses are equally plain. The machine is enormous, slow to work, slow to reload, and must be fixed on its bed, so the firing position has to be chosen in advance on high ground or aboard a gunboat, and the whole siege sequence is stretched accordingly. It has no capacity to breach a wall itself: breaking corner towers and gate towers and disrupting the deployment on the wall is the limit of what it can do, and the actual entry depends on ladders, rams, filled ditches and betrayal from within. The record of the assault at Lin'an is not detailed gate by gate, but what can be certain is that the siege train the Yuan brought down the river from Xiangyang and Ezhou was no different in composition from the one used at Xiangyang, and a heavy counterweight trebuchet must have been part of it. On the Song side the answer was bows and crossbows on the walls, logs and stones rolled down the parapets, rams against the gates, and gunpowder arrows and bombs; the tupo qiang described in the History of Song, a siege firearm tried out at Xiangyang that used gunpowder to drive a bolt, was still among the means with which the defenders answered siege engines and packed ranks. Outside the siege train the Yuan had Mongol wia bows, javelins, sabres, lamellar and mail armour, the bed crossbows and shenbi bows carried by the Han troops, and flat-bottomed sand boats, war junks and grain junks on the river, with ox carts and the relay stations of the zhi chi system moving goods inland.
tactics: 元軍的作戰是典型的分進合擊加先掃外圍。德祐元年秋，元軍取建康、鎮江之後，十月伯顏在鎮江分兵三路南攻，一路趨江西、兩路趨兩浙，同時讓阿里海牙取湖南以斷宋方從湖廣回援的可能，宋廷在江南的縱深因此被切成一條條斷線。宋廷的反應是組織勤王師北上拖延：張世傑所部在焦山水面列陣，試圖以水軍與上游水寨牽制元軍舟師，卻被火攻而潰，局勢從此一去不返。兵臨城下之後，元軍沒有立刻強攻，而是先取湖州、嚴州一線的屬州據點，掃清城郊，斷絕宋廷從兩浙腹地調兵的通道；同時把攻城器械與糧秣由船運抵江岸，砲位選在城外高處與泊於江心的砲舟上，壓制城頭角樓與門樓，等雲梯與撞竿可以接近時才發動總攻。守方則是多層拒止加上水陸互助：皇城、內城、外城三重城垣依序退守，弓弩手居高射擊，檑木、撞竿、拒馬應付破門，士兵趁夜出城焚毀攻城器械；城內河道縱橫，運河穿城而入，宋廷曾企圖以堵塞水道與封閉水門來阻止元軍舟楫直抵城下，卻也令自己的糧船難以入城。關鍵的轉折不在攻城而在談判與內應：賈似道遣使奉上國璽與降表想換取退兵，元軍不受，反責璽偽；破局者是范文虎，他以城降元，元軍得以在宋廷出降之後有秩序地入城，未遭大規模抵抗。伯顏入城時嚴禁士卒侵擾、准許降民繳錢贖身，士氣與秩序的反差，反而加深了南宋朝廷的崩潰速度。
tacticsEn: The Yuan's method was the classic combination of divided advance and clearing the outer ring first. In the autumn of the first year of Deyou, after taking Jianggan and Zhenjiang, Bayan divided his force at Zhenjiang in the tenth month into three columns marching south, one towards Jiangxi and two towards the Two Rivers, while Ariq Qoshqar took Hunan to close off any reinforcement the Song might draw from Huguang; the Song's depth in Jiangnan was thus cut into separate and broken lines. The Song answer was to gather relief columns and march north to slow the advance: the troops under Zhang Shijie were deployed on the water at Jiao Mountain in an attempt to pin the Yuan flotillas with their own ships and the river stockades upstream, but they were burned and routed, and from that moment the situation never came back. Once the army was under the walls it did not assault at once. It took the subordinate prefectures of Huzhou and Lin'an first, cleared the ground outside the walls, and cut the channels by which the court could draw troops from the interior of the Two Rivers; at the same time the siege engines and stores were brought up by boat to the bank, the gun positions were set on high ground outside the city and on gunboats moored mid-stream, and the corner towers and gate towers on the wall were beaten down so that ladders and rams could come in, the general assault being launched only when that was possible. The defence was a refusal in layers combined with mutual support by water and land: the three circuits — imperial city, inner city, outer city — were held in turn, bowmen and crossbowmen shot from above, logs, rams and spiked fences answered the battering at the gates, and men went out at night to burn the siege engines. The streets inside were cut by canals, the Grand Canal ran into the city, and the court tried to block the waterways and close the water gates to keep the Yuan boats from coming directly to the foot of the walls, which in turn made it hard to bring its own grain boats in. The turning point lay not in the assault but in negotiation and collusion from within: Jia Sidao offered the state seal and a letter of submission in the hope of buying a withdrawal; the Yuan refused and denounced the seal as false. What broke the city was Fan Wenhu, who surrendered it to the Yuan, so that after the court came out the Yuan could enter in good order without large-scale resistance. Bayan forbade his soldiers to rob on entering the city and allowed those who surrendered to redeem themselves by payment, and that contrast between order and collapse only deepened the speed with which the Song court came apart.
data: 可核實的數字集中在時間線與物資兩處。時間線：1275年元軍取建康府與鎮江府；同年十月伯顏於鎮江分兵三路南攻；1276年德祐二年正月至二月間元軍主力抵達臨安城下，圍城數月，至三月城破；1277年江浙等處行中書省設治於杭州；1279年崖山之役後南宋完全覆亡。圍城歷時約兩三個月，是正史記載中最具體的一段時程。兵船方面，張世傑部在焦山水面列陣，傳世史文記為「萬艘戰船」，此為宋代記帳式的概數，只宜當作量級看待；同一戰役中宋軍曾先後收復廣德軍、溧陽縣、常州等地，說明元軍推進並非一氣呵成。城防方面可以確定的是三重城垣與城內水道：外城沿錢塘江而建，皇城居中，內城、運河與縱橫河道互相貫通，宋廷曾以封堵水門與堵塞河道阻止元軍舟楫直抵城下。議和與出降的過程留下兩個關鍵數字：賈似道一方奉上傳國玉璽與降表，元軍不受並指璽為偽；出降之後，隨行北上的宋官屬、宮人、樂工及部分軍民，史稱以數十萬計，屬概數而非可點算之數。元軍兵員數在正史同樣多作「十餘萬」一類的概數，不宜深究；攻城砲的規格可由襄陽之役推知，回回砲所投之石重逾百斤，臨安之役的逐門紀錄則已散佚。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked sit in two places, the chronology and the materiel. On the chronology: in 1275 the Yuan took the prefectures of Jianggan and Zhenjiang; in the tenth month of the same year Bayan divided his force into three columns at Zhenjiang and marched south; between the first and second months of 1276, the first year of the Deyou era, the Yuan main force reached the foot of Lin'an's walls and lay there for some months before the city fell in the third; in 1277 the Jiangzhe Branch Secretariat was established with its seat at Hangzhou; and in 1279 the defeat at Yamen ended the Southern Song for good. The siege itself lasted something like two or three months, and this is the most securely datable span in the record. On ships and men: Zhang Shijie's fleet was deployed on the water at Jiao Mountain, which the historical text that survives for the battle of Lin'an gives as ten thousand war boats — a bookkeeping-style round figure of the Song, to be treated as an order of magnitude and nothing more. In the same campaign the Song recovered Guangde prefecture, Liyang county and Changzhou in turn, which shows that the Yuan advance was not accomplished in a single stroke. On the defences what can be certain is the triple circuit and the water system inside: the outer city ran along the Qiantang river, the imperial city sat in the middle, and the inner city, the Grand Canal and the branching streets were interconnected, and the court tried to close the water gates and block the channels to stop the Yuan boats coming directly to the walls. Two numbers matter from the negotiation and the surrender: the imperial seal and a letter of submission were handed over and refused, with the seal denounced as false; and after the surrender the Song officials, palace women, musicians and part of the army and populace who went north with the column are recorded in round numbers running to tens of thousands. The size of the Yuan army is likewise given only in general terms, in the official histories as something like more than a hundred thousand, and should not be pressed. The specification of the siege trebuchet can be inferred from Xiangyang, where the stones thrown by the huihui pao weighed more than a hundred jin; the gate-by-gate record of the assault at Lin'an has been lost.
cause: 打起來有四層。第一層是世仇：南宋自端平入洛（1234年）收復河南三州、襄鄂失而復得，就把自己放在與蒙古爭中原的位置上，杜車之爭（1260年代）之後，兩國在兩淮、荊襄一線的反覆拉鋸，把南方朝廷拖進了一場它既無力承擔、也無法退出的消耗戰；宋廷拒絕向元稱臣納幣，使雙方的和平從一開始就沒有基礎。第二層是元方的總戰略：忽必烈以漢地制度立國、以中原財賦養軍，滅宋不只是報復，更是把漠北草原的國家變成中國的正統；襄陽在1273年陷落，長江中游的門戶被打通之後，順流而下攻兩浙是必然的選擇。第三層是宋廷內部的應對失誤：右丞相賈似道主持的「端平入洛」政策本身就是與蒙古決裂的源頭，他又在咸淳十年（1274年）襄州失守之後久為遮掩，直到度宗死後才由內侍謝太后一系揭發，朝議為此分裂，軍心與輿論同時崩壞。第四層是談判與拖延的失敗：德祐元年冬賈似道遣使赴元營議和，雖暗奉國璽與降表，元軍不但不受，反指璽為偽，並繼續全線推進；宋廷以拖延換取援軍的盤算，隨著焦山之敗與各路勤王師的瓦解而徹底破滅，臨安遂成孤立之城。
causeEn: There were four layers behind the fighting. The first is the old feud: from the recovery of the Three Prefectures of Henan in 1234 and the taking and retaking of Xiangyang and Ezhou, the Southern Song had placed itself in the position of a power contesting the Central Plain with the Mongols, and after the clashes over the Two Rivers and the Huai region in the 1260s it was drawn into a war of attrition it could neither afford nor withdraw from; the court's refusal to address the Yuan as a vassal and pay tribute left the two states without any foundation for peace. The second is the Yuan's grand strategy: Kublai founded his state on the institutions of the Chinese land and fed his armies on the revenues of the Central Plain, and the destruction of the Song was not revenge so much as the conversion of a steppe power into the legitimate order of China; once Xiangyang fell in 1273 and the middle Yangtze was opened, marching down the river into the Two Rivers was the obvious choice. The third is the court's own misjudgements: the policy of the chancellor Jia Sidao, the recovery of the Central Plain, was itself the origin of the rupture with the Mongols, and after the loss of Xiangzhou in 1274 he concealed the news for years until it was exposed after the emperor's death, splitting the council and breaking the morale of the army and the confidence of the capital at one time. The fourth is the failure of negotiation and delay: in the winter of the first year of Deyou Jia Sidao sent envoys to treat, and even gave the state seal and a letter of submission behind their backs, and the Yuan not only refused them but denounced the seal as a forgery and kept advancing on every front; the calculation of buying time with a peace stalled and then ended, and with the defeat at Jiao Mountain and the dispersal of the relief columns the city of Lin'an was left isolated.
impact: 此役的直接後果是南宋中央政權的覆亡。臨安出降之後，元廷在1277年設江浙等處行中書省，治於杭州，把這座江南最大都市變成新朝的節度中樞；宋官爵秩與學校一度保留，漢人士大夫在失去國號之後多以「故宋遺民」自居，陳亮、辛棄疾一系北伐的理想中斷，文天祥、謝枋得則以力拒至死，把「忠」寫成南宋最後的道德遺產。臨安之役也改變了杭州的城市性格：元代杭州在江浙行省與江南航運樞紐的地位之下，商業與手工業續有發展，絲織、造船、瓷業與海運接上了泉州、明州的網絡，十三世紀末馬可孛羅抵達杭州，稱它是世上最富庶的城市之一，這段記述至今仍是當時歐洲人對中國南方最生動的印象。技術與軍事層面的教訓則是另一回事：元軍的攻城並非靠某一門砲取勝，而是靠封鎖、掃清外圍、砲火壓制、雲梯接近、招降內應的完整序列；配重投石車在這條序列裡是壓制城頭的重火力，卻從不負責破城。也正因為南宋朝廷在最後一年把希望全押在談判與拖延上，臨安才會在一次沒有大規模巷戰的投降中陷落。
impactEn: The immediate consequence was the destruction of the Southern Song's central government. After Lin'an came out, the Yuan court established the Jiangzhe Branch Secretariat in 1277 with its seat at Hangzhou, turning the largest city of Jiangnan into the pivot of the new dynasty; Song ranks and titles and the schools were for a time preserved, and scholar-officials who had lost the state name came to call themselves for the most part the surviving subjects of the former Song; the northern-recovery ideal carried by Chen Liang and Xin Qiji was broken off, while Wen Tianxiang and Xie Fangde refused to the death and turned loyalty into the last moral inheritance of the fallen dynasty. The battle also changed the character of the city itself. Under the Jiangzhe Branch Secretariat and as the hinge of the Jiangnan carrying trade, Hangzhou's commerce and handicrafts went on developing in the Yuan, with silk-weaving, shipbuilding, porcelain and the maritime trade linking into the network of Quanzhou and Mingzhou; when Marco Polo reached the city at the end of the thirteenth century he called it one of the richest cities on earth, and that passage remains the most vivid European impression of southern China of its age. The technical and military lesson is a different matter: the Yuan did not win through any single gun, but through a complete sequence of blockade, clearing the outer posts, artillery suppression, ladders coming in, and surrender and collusion from within; the counterweight trebuchet was the heavy fire that pinned the defenders to the wall, and it never had a hand in breaking the wall itself. And precisely because the Song court staked everything in the last year on negotiation and delay, Lin'an fell in a surrender that saw no great street fighting at all.
result: 結果是元軍入城，宋廷出降，中樞崩解。德祐二年三月，伯顏部抵達臨安，圍城數月，宋廷遣使議和被拒；守將范文虎以城降元，元軍得以入城，謝太后奉傳國璽與二王出降，宋恭帝隨元軍北行，皇城府庫為元軍所受。賈似道在議和破裂後棄軍逃揚州，為部將所誅；張世傑收拾散卒轉戰海上，終於崖山；文天祥在勤王之師潰散後被俘，拒不降，1283年死於大都；陸秀夫背宋少帝投海，南宋於1279年完全覆亡。從兵器角度看，這是一場「砲壓得住城頭、卻不曾破城」的戰役：配重投石車這類重型攻城器在江南攻城序列中負責的是獵殺角樓與城頭守軍、替雲梯與撞竿清出通道，真正的破城卻由范文虎開門與宋廷出降完成。元軍入城之後禁止掠奪、准許繳錢贖身、以行省接管兩浙，江南的行政、商業與手工業秩序在元代重新編排；南宋則在失去臨安之後只剩下海上兩王，數年之間也就走到了盡頭。
resultEn: The result was that the Yuan entered the city, the Song court came out and surrendered, and the central government came apart. In the third month of 1276, the second year of Deyou, Bayan's army reached Lin'an and lay around the walls for some months; the court's envoys were refused, and the commander Fan Wenhu surrendered the city to the Yuan, which allowed the army to enter, while Empress Dowager Xie came out with the state seal and the two princes, the child Emperor Gong was taken north with the Yuan columns, and the treasuries of the imperial city passed into their hands. After the negotiation collapsed Jia Sidao abandoned the army and fled to Yangzhou, where his own men killed him; Zhang Shijie gathered the scattered remnants and fought on at sea until Yamen; Wen Tianxiang, after the relief column was destroyed, was taken and refused to surrender, and was executed at Dadu in 1283; Lu Xiufu carried the young emperor into the sea, and by 1279 the Southern Song was entirely finished. Seen from the point of view of the weapons, this was a battle in which the artillery could pin the wall but never break it: the heavy counterweight trebuchets in the Yuan siege train did the work of hunting the corner towers and the defenders on the parapet and clearing a lane for the ladders and rams, while the actual entry was completed by Fan Wenhu opening the gates and the court walking out. After the Yuan entered, plunder was forbidden, the surrendered were allowed to redeem themselves by payment, and the Two Rivers were taken over by a branch administration; the administrative, commercial and handicraft order of Jiangnan was rearranged under the Yuan. The Song, having lost Lin'an, was left with only the two princes at sea, and within a few years came to its end.
